title: Affine comparison of an ideal-product intersection inclusion
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], F and G quasi-coherent O_X-modules [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], g:G \to F a monomorphism, I a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], U an affine open of X, and m,n nonnegative integers. Products and powers are the multiplication images and recursive powers of [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. Suppose I(U)^m F(U) \cap \operatorname{image}(g(U)) is contained in g(U)(I(U)^n G(U)). Then for every open W contained in U, the intersection of the section ranges of I^m F \to F and G \to F is contained in the section range of I^n G \to G \to F. There is no Noetherian, coherence, finiteness or existence-of-a-bound hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 01YA, affine reduction in the proof; Tags 01I8 and 01IC, tensor and exact affine sheaf comparison

proof.text: On U, the ideal powers and their multiplication images on F and G are quasi-coherent, and their section ranges identify with the ordinary ideal-power multiples, including power zero as the unit ideal.

Realize the intersection as the kernel of G -> F/(I^m F). The kernel and quotient are quasi-coherent. On U the section module of this kernel is the inverse image under g(U) of I(U)^m F(U); its image in F(U) is the stated intersection. The affine exact sheaf comparison identifies the inclusion into F with the inclusion of this section submodule.

The algebraic inclusion defines a linear factorization through the image of I(U)^n G(U). Under the affine module/sheaf correspondence from Tags 01I8 and 01IC this gives a factorization of the corresponding subsheaf inclusions. Restrict it to W. Sections in the two ranges define a section of the pullback intersection by its universal property. Applying the factorization gives a section of I^n G mapping to the original section. Thus the required range inclusion holds, including empty opens and zero exponents.

proof_origin.place: Fixed-exponent affine inclusion specialization of the geometric comparison in the proof of 01YA; no Artin-Rees or uniform bound used.

mathlib_searches.query: Affine quasi coherent sheaf inclusion of ideal products follows from inclusion of section submodules
Inclusion of quasi coherent submodules on an affine scheme is equivalent to inclusion of their global sections

theorem affine_ideal_intersection_inclusion {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (F G : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (g : G ⟶ F) [Mono g] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (U : X.affineOpens) (m n : ℕ)
    (hmodule : I.ideal U ^ m • (⊤ : Submodule Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1)) ⊓
        LinearMap.range (g.val.app (.op U.1)).hom ≤
      Submodule.map (g.val.app (.op U.1)).hom
        (I.ideal U ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule Γ(X, U.1) Γ(G, U.1)))) :
    ∀ W : X.Opens, W ≤ U.1 →
      Set.range ((idealModuleProductι (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).2 F).app W) ∩
          Set.range (g.app W) ⊆
        Set.range ((idealModuleProductι (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).2 G ≫ g).app W)
